name: Teutonic Order Moves Capital to Marienburg
summary: The Teutonic Order moves its Grand Master's seat from Venice to Marienburg (Malbork) in Prussia, completing the transformation of the crusading order into a territorial state. Marienburg castle, expanded continuously through the 14th century, becomes the largest Gothic brick castle in the world. The Order governs Prussia as a model of efficient administration, building roads, founding cities, and organizing agricultural colonization.

_quarry.structural_significance: Marienburg's construction as an administrative and military capital signals the Order's shift from crusading institution to territorial state; the Ordensstaat becomes one of the most efficiently governed states in medieval Europe, pioneering administrative techniques later adopted by the emerging national monarchies; its defeat at Grunwald (1410) and subsequent Peace of Thorn (1466) demonstrate that military orders cannot maintain state power against large kingdoms
